answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering works after the fact. The system clusters identities by shared timing patterns, device signals, and interaction rhythms, then audits any dense cluster as one operator. Each caught identity costs the attacker its accrued reputation and any opal rewards, since the whole cluster is penalized together. A single flagged vertex in that graph forces re-verification of every linked account. Rebuilding a trusted jade rating from scratch after a cluster collapse is the recurring cost, and it scales with how many accounts were run.
